name: Ramp
text: Add a high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. This fixes the biggest keyboard navigation pain point—users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one keystroke. The trade-off is a tiny extra markup cost, but it’s negligible compared to the universal benefit.

name: Reader
text: The skip link still fails if JavaScript loads late—users tab into a broken page and hit dead space. A server-rendered skip link with a real href="#main" and CSS to hide it until focus fixes the race, no JavaScript needed. Ship both versions behind a flag; measure tab-focus time to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Ship a server-rendered skip link as the single, non-negotiable option. It loads with the first 100 bytes of HTML, so keyboard users never wait for JavaScript—no race, no dead space, no broken tab order. The trade-off is a 20-byte anchor in every page, but that’s cheaper than debugging late-loading JS or explaining why half our users can’t navigate.

name: Reader
text: The server-rendered skip link risks locking us into a single solution that might not work for all users—what if someone’s assistive tech ignores the anchor or the page structure changes later? A hybrid approach: server-render the link but keep the JavaScript fallback as a safety net. Measure both by tracking how often users actually use the skip link—if the server version is ignored, we’ll know to scrap it.
